replacements.<span>Entrenar no basta: hace falta cicl: Training is not enough: you need the full lifecycle.
replacements.>Después despliegas, vigilas y vuelves a: >Then you deploy, monitor, and iterate again.
replacements.id: \"datos\", title: \"1) Datos — captu: id: "datos", title: "1) Data — capture signals", desc: "Here you collect the information that describes what is happening. Think of it as “taking notes” from the real world.", ex: "Each payment is stored with its clues: amount, country, merchant, time, device, history…", out: "A reliable dataset (tables) that represents reality.", risk: "If fields are missing or contain errors, the system learns badly and it becomes difficult to explain why it makes a decision."
replacements.id: \"preparar\", title: \"2) Preparar —: id: "preparar", title: "2) Prepare — organize and convert", desc: "You clean and convert the data into signals that are easy to use. It is like turning loose notes into a clear list of “clues”.", ex: "You create signals such as purchases in the last 24h, distance from usual places, or a change of phone.", out: "Variables/‘features’ ready for training and for exactly the same use in production.", risk: "If preparation differs between training and production, the model becomes inconsistent without you noticing."
replacements.id: \"entrenar\", title: \"3) Entrenar —: id: "entrenar", title: "3) Train — learn from examples", desc: "You teach the system with past cases so it can learn patterns. It learns through repetition.", ex: "With thousands of labeled payments, it learns which combinations usually end up being fraud.", out: "A model that returns a risk level for a given payment.", risk: "If there is bias or too few labels, it can learn the wrong rules."
replacements.id: \"evaluar\", title: \"4) Evaluar — c: id: "evaluar", title: "4) Evaluate — check before using it", desc: "You verify with data the model has not seen whether it really works and what errors it makes.", ex: "You measure detected fraud versus false positives (blocking legitimate people).", out: "Metrics + decision: a threshold for blocking, reviewing, or allowing a payment through.", risk: "Without evaluation, you can worsen the user experience or the business without realizing it."
replacements.id: \"registrar\", title: \"5) Versionar: id: "registrar", title: "5) Version — know what is running", desc: "You record everything so it can be reproduced or rolled back: model, data, code, and configuration.", ex: "The record says: “model v12, data through January, this code, and these parameters”.", out: "A traceable version (vX) and its associated model.", risk: "If there is an incident and you do not know which version is in production, fixing it becomes slow."
replacements.id: \"desplegar\", title: \"6) Desplegar: id: "desplegar", title: "6) Deploy — put it to work", desc: "You connect it to the real product and activate it in a controlled way, gradually when possible.", ex: "First it runs in ‘shadow’ mode (without making decisions), then you activate it for 5% of traffic.", out: "A production service that responds quickly and reliably.", risk: "An abrupt change can cause widespread blocking or incorrect decisions."
replacements.id: \"monitorizar\", title: \"7) Monitor: id: "monitorizar", title: "7) Monitor — watch over time", desc: "You check that the system continues to work well and that the data has not changed too much.", ex: "Alerts for latency, errors, costs, and pattern changes (drift).", out: "Dashboards and alerts for detecting degradation.", risk: "Degradation is often silent: the system works… but makes worse decisions."
replacements.id: \"feedback\", title: \"8) Feedback —: id: "feedback", title: "8) Feedback — learn from reality", desc: "When the ground truth arrives (confirmation), you use it to improve: retrain, adjust, or roll back.", ex: "Weeks later you confirm fraud/no fraud, and those cases feed the next training run.", out: "New correct examples for the next cycle.", risk: "Without feedback, the system becomes obsolete."
